facts.fact: DP step 6: identical optimizer step everywhere
Old DataParallel single-process single-node
DDP one process per GPU, multi-node, the baseline
DDP pros: simple, near linear scaling
DDP cons: full model + grads + optimizer on every GPU; the ceiling ZeRO/FSDP remove

facts.fact: 16 bytes per parameter: 2 bf16 weights + 2 bf16 grads + 12 fp32 master, momentum, variance, before activations
ZeRO shards these across the DP group instead of replicating

ZeRO-3 + shards parameters; all-gather each layer just in time in forward/backward, then free

ZeRO-Offload / ZeRO-Infinity push shards to CPU RAM / NVMe

facts.fact: FSDP2: composability with TP/PP/EP via device meshes
facts.phrase: composes with TP, PP and EP on a device mesh

facts.fact: FSDP2: sane state_dict handling through DCP
FSDP2: partial freezing works (LoRA-friendly)
FSDP2: ~7% lower memory, slightly better throughput than FSDP1
facts.where: Reading, ZeRO and FSDP (7% and 1.5%, reported)

facts.fact: 2026 default: FSDP2 over DeepSpeed on PyTorch unless NVMe offload; math identical, composition cleaner
facts.phrase: The arithmetic is the same; the composition is cleaner

facts.fact: HSDP: 2D mesh, FSDP-shard within a node, DDP-replicate across groups
facts.where: Reading, ZeRO and FSDP; animation HSDP

facts.fact: HSDP keeps all-gather on NVLink, only gradient all-reduce crosses nodes
facts.where: Reading, ZeRO and FSDP; animation HSDP (8.0 against 36.1 GB)
facts.phrase: only the gradient all-reduce crosses servers

facts.fact: HSDP bounds the blast radius of a failing node
HSDP when the model fits in one node's aggregate memory
facts.phrase: fits in one server's (or group's) aggregate memory

facts.fact: PP splits the model vertically into stages of consecutive layers, one stage per GPU or group
Naive PP idles GPUs: the bubble
Micro-batching plus a schedule hides most of it: GPipe, 1F1B, interleaved 1F1B, ZB-H1, DualPipe
Bubble fraction ~ (stages-1)/microbatches
facts.where: Reading, Pipeline; bubble table; animation PP

facts.fact: PP cheap on bandwidth, only activations cross stage boundaries; preferred cross-node split
facts.phrase: preferred way to split a model across servers

facts.fact: TP splits weight matrices horizontally (Megatron-LM)
TP column-parallel then row-parallel pairs in MLP and attention heads
TP all-reduces inside every layer
TP needs NVLink-class bandwidth; keep within a node; TP <= 8 typically
Sequence parallelism (Megatron-style) shards LayerNorm/dropout activations along sequence, removing duplicated activation memory
facts.where: Reading, Tensor parallelism and sequence parallelism

facts.fact: EP: distribute MoE experts across GPUs; tokens routed via all-to-all
EP: attention/dense parts replicated or sharded by other means
facts.phrase: stay replicated (data parallel) or are split another way

facts.fact: EP origin: Switch Transformers (corrected: GShard 2020 first; Switch simplified routing and studied the combinations)
EP modern practice: DeepSeek-V3, fine-grained experts, node-limited routing to cap all-to-all cost
EP modern practice: Qwen3-MoE
facts.where: Reading, Expert parallelism (config sourced; pretraining layout unconfirmed)

facts.fact: CP shards the sequence dimension of activations for long-context training; attention memory grows with sequence length
CP family: Ring Attention, KV blocks around a ring, overlapping compute and comms
CP family: DeepSpeed Ulysses, all-to-all so each GPU holds full sequence for a subset of heads
facts.phrase: full sequence for a subset of heads

facts.fact: Llama 3 used CP for its 128k-context phase
facts.where: Reading, Context; Composing table; calculator preset

facts.fact: torchtitan ships both (corrected: Ring Attention with all-gather rotation; Ulysses is DeepSpeed's)
Composing: DP (FSDP/HSDP) x PP x CP x TP(+SP), outermost to innermost, EP orthogonal
facts.phrase: DP (FSDP or HSDP) × PP × CP × TP (+SP)

facts.fact: Rule: fit the model first: FSDP alone up to tens of B; add TP when a layer no longer fits or FSDP comms dominate; PP across nodes for 100B+ (corrected to the Playbook's own thresholds)
facts.where: Reading, Composing rules and correction box
facts.phrase: Under 10B parameters one technique is enough

facts.fact: Rule: add CP only for long sequences; EP for MoE
facts.phrase: Add CP across nodes for very long sequences

facts.fact: Rule: keep TP and EP dispatch inside NVLink domains; PP and DP gradient sync across InfiniBand
Rule: then scale batch via DP and gradient accumulation to hit the target global batch
facts.phrase: Then reach the target global batch

facts.fact: Activation checkpointing trades ~30% compute (corrected: full 30-40%, selective about 2.7%)
facts.where: Reading, Activation checkpointing and correction box

facts.fact: Selective checkpointing (attention only) is the usual sweet spot with FlashAttention
torchtitan: PyTorch-native pretraining reference; FSDP2 + TP + PP + CP
torchtitan: torch.compile, fp8 (now MXFP8 and NVFP4), DCP checkpointing, torchft fault tolerance
Megatron-Core / NeMo: NVIDIA's production stack; most mature TP/PP kernels
facts.phrase: most mature TP and PP kernels

facts.fact: DeepSpeed: still relevant for ZeRO-Offload/Infinity and HF Trainer integration
nanotron: HF's lightweight pretraining lib, Playbook companion
FSDP2 + HSDP covers most fine-tuning and sub-70B pretraining; full 4D only at frontier scale
facts.phrase: full 4D parallelism is needed only at frontier scale
